claim: Orion Cloud's reported quarterly capex exceeds the sum of its two rounded components by USD 1 billion.

evidence.text: Fictional Orion Cloud management reported total Q2 FY2026 capex of USD 34 billion.
Fictional Orion Cloud management described Q2 FY2026 components as approximately USD 27 billion cash property outlays and USD 6 billion of finance-lease additions; figures are rounded.

expected.rationale: 34-(27+6)=1 on the stated rounded figures. The claim does not invent a cause or force an exact accounting bridge.

claim: This packet establishes final customer AI spending of USD 180 million by adding Helix Chips sales to Vector Servers sales.

evidence.text: Fictional Helix Chips sold USD 60 million of accelerators to Vector Servers during FY2025.
Fictional Vector Servers incorporated those accelerators into systems it sold to final customers for USD 120 million during FY2025. No other sales are in this packet.

expected.rationale: Adding an intermediate sale to the final system sale double counts the shared supply chain; the supplied final-customer sale is120.

claim: Aurora Power's USD 90 million FY2026 profit outlook is still its current guidance at the cutoff.

evidence.text: Fictional Aurora Power forecast FY2026 profit of USD 90 million on May 1, 2026.
On June 10, 2026, fictional Aurora Power withdrew its prior FY2026 profit guidance and issued no replacement.

expected.rationale: The later eligible withdrawal supersedes the original outlook for a claim about current guidance.

claim: Nova Applications has higher FY2025 revenue in US dollars than Pulsar Software.

evidence.text: Fictional Nova Applications reported FY2025 revenue of EUR 80 million.
Fictional Pulsar Software reported FY2025 revenue of USD 82 million. No exchange rate or translated Nova revenue is supplied.

expected.rationale: The packet does not supply a currency conversion, so the dollar revenue ordering is undetermined.

claim: Meridian Networking's reported FY2025 shares for its two named customers sum to 50%.

evidence.text: Fictional Meridian Networking reports that Northstar represented 31% and Equinox 19% of its FY2025 revenue. These are distinct customers.

expected.rationale: 31%+19%=50%, and the source explicitly distinguishes the two customers.

claim: After deducting cash PP&E and lease interest from operating cash flow, Zenith Cooling has USD 18 million remaining; this avoids double counting.

evidence.text: Fictional Zenith Cooling reported FY2025 operating cash flow of USD 50 million, which already includes USD 2 million of lease-interest payments, and separate cash PP&E outlays of USD 30 million.

expected.rationale: The extra subtraction repeats an expense already included in operating cash flow; the nonduplicated cash remainder is20.

claim: Lyra Data Centers recognized more than USD 10 million of FY2026 revenue from its newly signed contracts.

evidence.text: Fictional Lyra Data Centers signed USD 45 million of new contracts in FY2026. Service starts may fall in FY2026 or FY2027. No contract revenue recognized in either year is disclosed.

expected.rationale: Contract value and possible service windows do not determine recognized FY2026 revenue.

claim: At the cutoff, the eligible statement reports Solstice Fabrication FY2025 company operating cash flow as USD 72 million.

evidence.text: Fictional Solstice Fabrication reported FY2025 company operating cash flow of USD 72 million.
Fictional Solstice Fabrication corrected FY2025 operating cash flow to USD 68 million.

expected.rationale: The claim is explicitly about the eligible statement at the cutoff; the later correction is ineligible and must not be cited.
